sample.pageIntro: Sample sets to verify the format and quality of data captured with the RootLens iOS app. New versions will be added as recording conditions and contributor scale expand.
sample.heroSubtitle: 48 first-person video clips of household tasks with per-frame 3D hand pose, wrist 6-DoF actions, and natural-language action labels.
sample.s1p1Lead: 48 clips of household tasks recorded with the RootLens iOS app from a head-mounted camera in Japan. All faces are blurred. Each frame contains:
s1p1Items: 21 hand joints in 3D per hand, in MANO canonical hand-local coordinates (`observation.hand_keypoints_3d`)
`task_index` into `meta/tasks.jsonl` pointing to a natural-language action label
sample.s2p1: LeRobotDataset v3.0 format. Standard loaders read this layout without modification.
sample.s3p1: Each frame's `task_index` maps to an action label in `meta/tasks.jsonl`. Labels are present-tense English sentences describing hand movements and objects (e.g. "Right hand reaches for the kettle handle."). Each clip is segmented into multiple labels at action transitions.
sample.s3p2: Labels are generated from video frames by a vision-language model.
sample.episodesSubheading: All 48 episodes. Click to play; expand a panel to read every action label with its timestamp.
sample.s4p1Lead: The next sample will add captures from roughly a dozen Japan-based TestFlight beta contributors:
s4p1Items: `observation.state` : camera 6-DoF in the ARKit world frame
`depth/{frame_index:06d}.png` : LiDAR depth maps on supported devices

hero.description: RootLens is a physical-AI project born at the University of Osaka. We monetize work data from Japan's commercial workplaces and return the benefits, in many forms, to the workplaces themselves.

problem.title: Robots learn by watching people. Nobody is collecting the footage.
problem.p1: Teaching a robot to work takes a huge amount of video of people actually working. Just as ChatGPT learned language from a vast amount of text, robots learn human motion from a vast amount of video.
problem.p2: But usable work footage is in critically short supply. Billions of people do this kind of work every day, all over the world, yet there is no infrastructure that collects it as data. A precious resource is being thrown away unused.
problem.p3: The data that works is produced in the course of everyday operations, on site.

services.title: Services that help the workplace, concretely

appFlow.label: SERVICE 01 · FOR EMPLOYERS
appFlow.title: Part-timers that pay you back
appFlow.intro: For any workplace that hires part-timers: restaurants, retail, light warehouse work. Hire a RootLens staffer wearing a headgear camera as a regular part-timer; we sell the footage recorded on shift as training data and return a filming fee for the hours recorded.

step1.label: Work as usual
step1.text: Staff wearing a headgear camera work part-time shifts. Dishwashing, prep, stocking, packing: any line of work is fine, as long as the headgear and the filming aren't in the way.

step2.label: Footage becomes training data
step2.text: The close-up work footage staff record on shift becomes valuable training data that teaches robots how to move. The data is never used for anything outside AI and robotics R&D.

step3.label: The workplace gets paid
step3.text: We pay a filming fee for the hours recorded: the workplace keeps the extra hands while holding labor costs down. The fee also goes to the staff themselves, adding a few hundred yen to their effective hourly wage.

math.note: Example at a ¥1,200 hourly wage. The fee is paid per recorded hour. ¥500 is the current base rate; we raise it as data sales grow, aiming for zero effective cost.

enterprise.label: SERVICE 02 · FOR COMPANIES
enterprise.title: Start with a workplace diagnostic
enterprise.p1: For companies considering robots or physical AI. We bring the capture equipment and app, record the work on your floor, and deliver a diagnostic report, free of charge: which steps suit automation and what adoption would take.
enterprise.p2: It can be free because only the data you approve is sold as training data, and that revenue covers the diagnostic. All we ask of the site is the recording.

model.label: HOW IT WORKS
model.title: We sell the work data collected on site, and the revenue funds services that help the workplace.
model.p1: Work data has buyers. Robotics companies are searching worldwide for training footage. But it is not realistic for a shop or a factory to sell its own data.
model.p2: So RootLens takes it all on, from filming to the sale. The revenue then goes back as a service shaped to what each workplace struggles with. For stores short on hands: staff who record while they work, plus a filming fee. For companies weighing automation: a free workplace diagnostic. More ways to give back will follow.
model.p3: All we ask of the workplace: keep working as usual.
model.emphasis: Global physical AI on one side, Japanese industry on the other. RootLens is building the crossing point.

devices.label: FOR DATA BUYERS
devices.title: Capture rigs and data specs
devices.intro1: Robot training can't use just any video. It needs footage focused on the work itself, shot in real environments, from as many different sites as possible. RootLens data is collected in shops and workplaces that are actually in business. Every clip is checked with the site where it was filmed, and only clips the site has consented to are uploaded.
devices.intro2: We grow the lineup rig by rig; one set is in operation today. See the sample data for format details.

set01.s6v: Single nanosecond timebase across all sensors
set01.s7v: Included with every clip (RGB and depth)
